author: 66six11
text:
[Slice] Foundation: define package factory, scope, and lifecycle contracts

## Parent and integration context

- Parent: #264
- Continues the secondary foundation integration chain from #283 / local commit `d4f1ca9a`.
- This Slice is not intended to merge directly to `main`; it remains a PR-sized checkpoint on the long-running refactor branch chain.

## Goal

Define the author-owned Factory / Scope / Lifecycle input contract required before a deterministic Activation Plan or Host Runtime can be implemented.

The contract must answer:

- which logical factories a package module contributes;
- which scope owns each factory instance;
- which other factories are required;
- which declared package contributions each factory activates;
- which fixed lifecycle model the future Host Runtime will enforce.

## Architecture decisions

- Add a separate `asharia.package.factories.json` author sidecar with schema `com.asharia.package-factories` v1.
- Keep the installable manifest portable: no CMake target, artifact path, dynamic-library path, C++ symbol, ABI, or callback name enters this contract.
- Factory IDs are logical package-local identities; future generated composition roots bind them to statically linked code.
- Scope is a lifetime owner, not a service-locator namespace.
- Lifecycle is host-defined and fixed: create → activate → quiesce → deactivate → destroy. Packages do not invent phases or failure policy.
- Required factory dependencies form a graph distinct from package/module selection order.
- Every installable-manifest module is covered explicitly, including `no-factories`; every declared contribution is claimed exactly once by a factory in its owner module.
- Candidate Discovery snapshots exact sidecar bytes and integrity; Locked Verification revalidates binding and bytes before future planning.

## Scope

- JSON Schema and semantic validation for Package Factory Declaration v1.
- Canonical normalization/rendering and contract-kind dispatch.
- Author-manifest/package binding validation.
- Local factory-reference, cycle, scope-direction, direct-package-dependency, and contribution-ownership validation.
- Candidate Discovery snapshot and TOCTOU protection.
- Locked Verification revalidation.
- Effective Session verified-candidate handoff preservation.
- Positive/negative tests and architecture/workflow documentation.

## Non-goals

- Activation Plan generation or execution.
- Host Runtime, scope objects, factory contexts, leases, rollback implementation, or UI.
- Dynamic plugin loading, hot unload/reload, stable C++ ABI, DLL symbols, artifact selection, or CMake generation.
- Optional/soft dependencies, author-defined phases, arbitrary singleton/transient lifetimes, or thread-affinity policy.
- ImGui/Avalonia bootstrap UI work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Declaration schema is closed, versioned, deterministic, and repository-validated.
- [x] Factory IDs are package-unique; module coverage is exact.
- [x] Local required-factory references exist, are acyclic, and obey same/ancestor scope ownership.
- [x] External requirements name only the package itself or a direct author-manifest dependency.
- [x] Contributions are known and claimed exactly once by a factory in the manifest-declared owner module.
- [x] Candidate Discovery snapshots parsed data, exact bytes, and integrity and rejects mid-scan mutation.
- [x] Locked Verification rejects missing, changed, or rebound declarations.
- [x] Effective Session handoff preserves the verified declaration snapshot.
- [x] Documentation freezes lifecycle/failure semantics and explicitly separates this contract from executable Activation Plans.
- [x] Full validation and dual-compiler pre-commit gates pass.

## Validation

- Package contract/discovery/lock/effective-session Python suites.
- Repository package-contract and topology checks.
- Text encoding and `git diff --check`.
- `clangcl-debug` and `msvc-debug` builds after Conan bootstrap/environment setup.

## Evidence

- O3DE Gem Modules expose fixed module initialization/create/destroy entry points and use static modules in monolithic builds: https://docs.o3de.org/docs/user-guide/programming/gems/overview/
- O3DE System Components use activate/deactivate and required services to order dependencies: https://docs.o3de.org/docs/user-guide/programming/components/system-components/
- Unreal documents that module loading order inside a phase is not deterministic, so explicit dependencies remain necessary: https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-modules

## Done evidence

Record the commit, changed contract/docs, exact test commands/results, and any remaining gap before closing. Use `Refs #284` until every acceptance criterion is satisfied.

author: lkaliturin220-svg
text:
🔴 Полное Code Review: Безопасность, Архитектура, Качество кода

## Полное Code Review: BusEngine (BuslikDrev/BusEngine)

**Автор:** [БуслікДрэў](https://buslikdrev.by/)  
**Лицензия:** MIT  
**Язык:** C# (.NET Framework 4.7.1+, netstandard2.0)  
**Размер репозитория:** ~250MB (включая бинарники MSBuild + документацию)  
**Строк C# кода:** ~23,000  

---

## 🔴 CRITICAL — Безопасность

### 1. RCE (Remote Code Execution) через Process.Start из браузера

**Файл:** `BusEngine/Code/Plugin/Program.cs`, строка 151

```csharp
} else if (t == "_linkgo|") {
    System.Diagnostics.Process.Start(message.Substring(8));
```

Сообщение `message` приходит из встроенного CefSharp-браузера через колбэк `OnPostMessage`. **Любая** веб-страница, загруженная в движок, может выполнить произвольный процесс на хосте пользователя. Достаточно чтобы JavaScript внутри игры отправил `_linkgo|cmd.exe /c ...` — и команда выполнится.

**Степень опасности:** полный контроль над машиной пользователя.  
**Исправление:** whitelist разрешённых URL/протоколов, НЕ передавать сырой пользовательский ввод в `Process.Start`.

Аналогичная проблема в шаблонах:
- `Templates/cs/Launcher/Code/Plugin/Program.cs:132` 
- `Templates/cs/CubesOpenGL/Code/CubesOpenGL/Program.cs:1913` (более безопасный вариант с `ProcessStartInfo`, но всё равно без валидации)

### 2. WMI Injection

**Файл:** `BusEngine/Code/BusEngine/BusEngine.cs`, строка 2555

```csharp
query.Query = new ObjectQuery(
    "SELECT * FROM Win32_LogicalDisk WHERE Name='" + 
    BusEngine.Engine.EngineDirectory.Substring(0, 2) + "' OR Name='" + 
    BusEngine.Engine.EditorDirectory.Substring(0, 2) + "'");
```

Конкатенация непроверенных путей в WMI-запрос. Если злоумышленник контролирует `EngineDirectory` или `EditorDirectory` — возможно внедрение произвольного WMI-запроса.

### 3. `fixgithub.cs` — 11,177 строк ASCII-арта, 0 строк кода

**Файл:** `BusEngine/Code/fixgithub.cs` — 1.7 MB.

Файл содержит **12+ копий ASCII-логотипа** в блочных комментариях и **ни одной строки кода**. Ни классов, ни неймспейсов, ни `using`. Это мёртвый груз, который:
- Замедляет компиляцию (компилятор всё равно парсит комментарии)
- Увеличивает размер репозитория на 1.7 MB
- Засоряет поиск по коду

**Рекомендация:** удалить немедленно.

---

## 🔴 HIGH — Архитектурные проблемы

### 4. God Object: `BusEngine.cs` — 10,105 строк, 50+ классов в одном файле

Один файл содержит: Engine, AI, Audio, Browser, Camera, Canvas, Color, Core, FlowGraph, Layer, Level, Localization, Log, Material, Matrix2-4x3, Model, Object, Physics, Plugin, Rendering, Shader, Ajax, Json, File, Timer, Canvas (UI), Vector2-4, Video, ProjectDefault, Device, Form, IPlugin...

**Проблемы:**
- Невозможно тестировать изолированно (0 unit-тестов)
- Навигация по файлу занимает минуты даже в IDE
- Любое изменение рискует сломать несвязанный функционал
- Когнитивная нагрузка на новых контрибьюторов запредельна
- Класс-заглушка `internal class G` (строка 6759) — невнятное имя

### 5. Массовое дублирование кода

| Файл | Строк | Идентичен |
|------|-------|-----------|
| `Game/Game.cs` | 278 |  |
| `Editor/Editor.cs` | 274 | ✨ 99% |

Различаются только:
- GUID мьютекса (`0968cb8e...` vs `28cb03ec...`)  
- `Engine.Platform` (`"Windows"` vs `"WindowsEditor"`)

Шаблоны (`Launcher/Code/Plugin/Program.cs` и `Plugin/Program.cs`) также содержат идентичную логику обработки `OnPostMessage`.

**Исправление:** вынести общий `Initialize` + `Form` в shared library.

### 6. Зашитые API-ключи

**Файл:** `Plugin/Program.cs`, строки 119-121

```csharp
System.Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("google_api_key", "123");
System.Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("google_default_client_id", "123.apps.googleusercontent.com");
System.Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("google_default_client_secret", "123-123");
```

Хотя значения сейчас заглушки, сам паттерн опасен. API-ключи не должны храниться в коде.

### 7. Принудительный GC.Collect на таймере

**Файл:** `BusEngine.cs`, строки 3043-3045

```csharp
System.GC.Collect();
System.GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
System.GC.Collect();  // ДВАЖДЫ подряд!
```

Каждые N секунд (по умолчанию 5) вызывается принудительная сборка мусора — дважды. Это симптом проблем с управлением памятью, а не решение. Вызывает фризы рендеринга.

---

## 🟡 MEDIUM — Качество кода

### 8. Чрезмерное использование `dynamic` — 35 вхождений

Все колбэки Ajax-класса принимают `dynamic`:
```csharp
public delegate void Success(dynamic data = null, dynamic xhr = null);
public delegate void Error(dynamic xhr = null, string textStatus = null, dynamic thrownError = null);
```

Теряется типобезопасность. Исключения во время исполнения вместо ошибок компиляции.

### 9. 512 операторов `new` — GC pressure

Множество аллокаций на каждый кадр — включая `Paint`-обработчик. При 60 FPS = ~30,000 `new`/сек — серьёзная нагрузка на GC.

### 10. Проблемы многопоточности

- **28 try / 14 catch** — половина блоков try без обработчиков исключений (компилятор не требует catch при finally, но здесь и finally используется неконсистентно)
- **Статические мутабельные поля:** `Commands`, `FPSCPU`, `FPSGPU`, `FPSKEY` — гонки данных
- **`Task.Factory.StartNew` без `ConfigureAwait`** — deadlock-риск в UI-контексте
- **Три копии плагин-лоадера** (строки 5854-5953) — отличается только `typ` (1/2/3), выбор захардкожен (`typ = 3`)

### 11. Нарушение IDisposable — 43 ручных `.Dispose()`

Вместо `using` — ручные вызовы `.Dispose()`. При исключении ресурсы утекают:
```csharp
System.Threading.Tasks.Task[] tasks = ...;
// ... работа с tasks ...
foreach (System.Threading.Tasks.Task tt in tasks) {
    tt.Dispose();  // утечёт если исключение до этого
}
```

### 12. Строковая конкатенация в циклах — 176 `+=`

Порождает множество промежуточных строк. Нужен `StringBuilder`.

### 13. Отладочный код в релизе — 124 вызова `Console.*`

`Console.WriteLine`, `Console.Beep()` — должны быть под `#if DEBUG`.

### 14. `Environment.Exit(0)` в Shutdown

```csharp
public static void ShutdownStatic(bool nagibator = false) {
    // ...
    if (nagibator) {
        System.Environment.Exit(0);  // жёсткое убийство процесса
    }
}
```

Параметр с игривым названием `nagibator`. `Environment.Exit` не даёт выполниться финализаторам и `finally`-блокам.

### 15. Unsafe P/Invoke без обработки ошибок

```csharp
[DllImport("ntdll.dll", SetLastError = true)]
private static extern bool NtSetTimerResolution(...);
```

Вызывается без проверки `Marshal.GetLastWin32Error()`. При ошибке таймер может работать неверно без диагностики.

---

## 🟢 LOW — Стиль и документация

| Проблема | Детали |
|----------|--------|
| Закомментированный код | ~30% кодовой базы — мёртвый код в комментариях |
| Белорусские комментарии | Ограничивает международный вклад |
| 0 тестов | При 23K строк кода — любой рефакторинг рискован |
| Нет README | Отсутствует описание, инструкции по сборке |
| `internal class G` | Заглушка с бессмысленным именем |
| Игровые названия | `nagibator`, `Шедевр.busproject` в параметрах |
| CefSharp зависимость | ~100MB+ бинарников в репозитории |

---

## 📊 Сводная таблица метрик

| Метрика | Значение |
|---------|----------|
| Строк C# кода | ~23,000 |
| Строк в fixgithub.cs (мусор) | 11,177 |
| Классов в одном файле | 50+ |
| `new` аллокаций | 512 |
| `dynamic` использований | 35 |
| `try` без `catch` | 14 |
| IDisposable без `using` | 43 |
| Console.* в коде | 124 |
| Task.Factory.StartNew | 12 |
| GC.Collect() принудительно | 2× каждые 5 сек |
| RCE-уязвимостей | 1 (подтверждено) |
| WMI-инъекций | 1 |
| Unit-тестов | 0 |

---

## 🔧 Приоритетный план исправлений

### Критические (немедленно)
1. ❌ **Удалить `fixgithub.cs`** — 1.7MB мусора
2. ❌ **RCE Fix** — whitelist URL в `Process.Start` или полный запрет запуска процессов из браузера
3. ❌ **WMI Injection Fix** — параметризованные запросы или санитизация путей

### Высокий приоритет
4. **Вынести общий код Game/Editor** в базовый класс
5. **Убрать `GC.Collect()`** — найти утечки через memory profiler
6. **Убрать `Environment.Exit()`** — заменить на нормальный shutdown
7. **Перенести API-ключи**

[BUG] linux_arm64/libcef.so is built as x86-64 binary, causing crash on aarch64 systems

### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I have searched through existing issues and confirmed this bug has not been reported yet.
- [x] I have reproduced this on the latest development build.

### LiquidBounce Branch

Nextgen

### LiquidBounce Build/Version

0.37.0

### Operating System

Linux

### Minecraft Version

Fabric 1.21.11

### Describe the bug

On aarch64 systems, LiquidBounce downloads and extracts MCEF successfully 
(checksum passes), but the extracted linux_arm64/libcef.so is actually an 
x86-64 binary, causing an UnsatisfiedLinkError crash at startup.

This was confirmed using the `file` command:
  linux_arm64/libcef.so: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64

The file is 230MB and not corrupted — it is simply the wrong architecture.
This is a regression of issue #2291, which was previously closed as fixed.

Verified using the `file` command that the downloaded libcef.so is x86-64:
nolan@raspberrypi:~ $ file ~/.local/share/PrismLauncher/instances/Fabulously\ Optimized/minecraft/LiquidBounce/mcef/libraries/9bd969a508d52a150f42ac1baebece2c7cdcf66d/linux_arm64/libcef.so /home/nolan/.local/share/PrismLauncher/instances/Fabulously Optimized/minecraft/LiquidBounce/mcef/libraries/9bd969a508d52a150f42ac1baebece2c7cdcf66d/linux_arm64/libcef.so: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, BuildID[sha1]=1ffba217944954b6fc9eeae7b8b8190870e8d135, stripped nolan@raspberrypi: $

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run LiquidBounce on a Linux aarch64 system (e.g. Raspberry Pi 5)
2. Allow MCEF to download and extract on first launch
3. Client crashes at the main menu with UnsatisfiedLinkError
4. Run: file ~/.local/share/PrismLauncher/instances/.../LiquidBounce/mcef/libraries/9bd969a508d52a150f42ac1baebece2c7cdcf66d/linux_arm64/libcef.so

text:
Advanced observability connector fabric, debug mode, and OpenHuman-style knowledge tree

Parent: #167
Related: #137, #170, #172, #175

## Goal
Build the next-generation observability layer for Control One: a connector fabric that is broader and smarter than a traditional SIEM connector catalog, with first-class DBMS/application-framework instrumentation, log-driven auto-detection, safe fallback paths, temporary deep debug mode, and a highly friendly operator UI.

This should not become a pile of one-off connectors. The product should make the common path radically simple:

- App frameworks: add one error-handling service registration, middleware, package, or agent hook and Control One gets structured errors, request context, traces, framework metadata, dependency failures, and safe remediation hints.
- DBMS: onboard each database with a root/master or highly privileged bootstrap credential when needed, then discover audit/log/profiler surfaces, generate least-privilege collector grants, and downgrade ongoing collection to scoped roles wherever possible.
- Missing instrumentation: use robust log-driven auto-detection and fallback so a detected app/DB still yields useful coverage through logs, process inventory, network flows, config files, DB audit discovery, and side-channel evidence.
- Debug mode: temporarily increase verbosity across DBMS, webservers, and app frameworks with TTL, scope, rollback, redaction, budgets, and audit receipts.
- Knowledge base: adopt the OpenHuman memory/knowledge architecture as the Control One knowledge layer so investigations and AI answers are grounded in deterministic, readable, source-linked memory, not opaque vector soup.

## Research Notes
References checked while drafting:

- Microsoft Sentinel data connector catalog: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference
  - Sentinel exposes a large Content Hub connector catalog, solution-backed connectors, community connectors, and custom connector paths. Control One must beat this by combining connector breadth with native app/DB instrumentation, auto-detection, and clear coverage truth.
- OpenHuman source reviewed at commit `65d92bf10a834c2a540ff67a302f89963bd35d56`: https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman
- OpenHuman Memory Tree docs: https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/blob/main/gitbooks/features/obsidian-wiki/memory-tree.md
- OpenHuman auto-fetch docs: https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/blob/main/gitbooks/features/obsidian-wiki/auto-fetch.md
- OpenHuman Obsidian-style memory docs: https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/blob/main/gitbooks/features/obsidian-wiki/README.md
- OpenHuman agentmemory backend docs: https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/blob/main/gitbooks/features/obsidian-wiki/agentmemory-backend.md
- OpenHuman TokenJuice docs: https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/blob/main/gitbooks/features/token-compression.md

OpenHuman architecture elements to adopt exactly in spirit and contract:

- Deterministic ingest pipeline: source adapters -> canonical Markdown + provenance -> <=3k-token chunks with deterministic IDs -> atomic Markdown content store -> SQLite-backed chunks/scores/summaries/jobs -> score + embeddings + entity extraction -> source/topic/global summary trees -> retrieval.
- Three tree scopes: source trees per source, topic trees per hot entity, and global daily digests.
- Durable async jobs: `extract_chunk`, `append_buffer`, `seal`, `topic_route`, `digest_daily`, and `flush_stale`, with retry/dedupe/lease recovery.
- Chunk lifecycle: `pending_extraction -> admitted -> buffered -> sealed`, with a `dropped` branch that preserves provenance but excludes low-signal content from summary trees.
- Local/readable vault: every chunk and summary exists as Markdown in an Obsidian-compatible `wiki/` vault with frontmatter provenance.
- Retrieval that can search, drill down, fetch source chunks, and cite provenance.
- Auto-fetch pattern: one scheduler loop walks active connections, per-connection sync state tracks cursor/budget/dedupe/last sync, errors are logged without killing the scheduler.
- Token compression before LLM context so high-volume logs/traces/tool output stay affordable and useful.

Control One adaptation: Doris remains the high-volume event lake. The OpenHuman-style Memory Tree becomes the curated, deterministic, human-readable investigation and knowledge layer over logs, traces, connector output, cases, remediation receipts, posture changes, and operator notes.

## Problem Statement
Traditional SIEM connector breadth is necessary but not enough. Sentinel-like connector catalogs still rely heavily on operators finding the right connector, granting access, wiring logs, and knowing what is missing. Control One should feel smarter:

1. Discover apps, DBMS, webservers, queues, caches, runtimes, and cloud services automatically.
2. Offer a one-line or low-friction instrumentation path for every supported app framework.
3. Offer DBMS bootstrap onboarding that can use master/root access safely but produces least-privilege ongoing collection whenever possible.
4. Fall back to logs, network/process evidence, config files, and side-channel inference when direct instrumentation is absent.
5. Tell the operator exactly what is covered, missing, partial, or unsafe.
6. Let operators enable temporary deep debug traces without permanently changing production verbosity or leaking secrets.
7. Store investigative knowledge in an OpenHuman-style memory architecture so AI and humans can retrieve, inspect, edit, and cite the knowledge base.

## Workstreams

### 1. Observability Connector Fabric
Create a versioned connector framework that avoids bespoke logic scattered across the codebase.

Required capabilities:

- Define connector/provider interfaces for `app_framework`, `dbms`, `webserver`, `load_balancer`, `queue`, `cache`, `runtime`, `cloud_service`, `identity`, `saas`, and `custom_log`.
- Every connector declares capabilities: inventory, native instrumentation, log paths, parser support, audit support, trace support, debug-mode support, remediation bindings, required privileges, fallback paths, fixture status, and safety class.
- Add a connector manifest model that can power docs, UI, tests, and AI tool selection.
- Add support states: `unsupported`, `detected_only`, `log_only`, `raw_only`, `normalized`, `instrumented`, `audit_connected`, `debug_supported`, `remediation_supported`, `degraded`, and `needs_access`.
- Connect this to the coverage truth layer from #167 so unsupported services are never shown as green.

### 2. App Framework One-Line Instrumentation
For each supported framework, provide the simplest possible integration primitive: middleware, error handler, service registration, decorator, package, or OpenTelemetry-compatible hook.

Initial framework targets:

- Node.js: Express, NestJS, Next.js, Fastify, Koa, Hapi, PM2/runtime error hooks.
- Python: Django, Flask, FastAPI, Starlette, Celery, Gunicorn, Uvicorn.
- Java/JVM: Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut, Play, Vert.x, servlet filters for Tomcat/Jetty/WildFly/WebLogic/WebSphere paths.
- .NET: ASP.NET Core/Kestrel, IIS-hosted ASP.NET, EF Core exception/query hooks.
- PHP: Laravel, Symfony, WordPress/PHP-FPM where feasible.
- Ruby: Rails, Rack, Puma, Sidekiq.
- Go: net/http, Gin, Echo, Fiber, chi.

Each framework package should capture:

- exception/error class, message fingerprint, stack fingerprint, route/controller/action, request ID, trace ID, correlation ID, tenant/application/service identity, deployment version, runtime version, dependency call failures, DB query fingerprint when available, sanitized request metadata, and severity.
- redaction before transport, with secrets/PII denylist and allowlist support.
- graceful fallback to log parsing when app-level instrumentation is absent.
- documented install snippets that the UI can show as copy/paste cards.

### 3. DBMS Bootstrap, Audit, And Fallback
Support master/root or equivalent privileged on

text:
[BUG]: Baggage accumulates across unrelated Hangfire jobs

### Tracer Version(s)

3.44.0

### Operating system and platform

Linux arm64

### Instrumentation Mode

automatic

### TFM

net8.0

### Bug Report

#### `Baggage.Current` accumulates across sequential Hangfire jobs, causing oversized `baggage` headers on downstream HTTP calls                                                                                                   

### Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
   
When using the Hangfire integration with W3C baggage propagation enabled (the default in v3.x),                                                                                                                                 
`Baggage.Current` appears to grow monotonically across sequential jobs processed by the same worker. Each job's baggage is merged into whatever ambient state already exists rather than replacing it, so jobs accumulate entries from all prior jobs on that worker.
The result is that outbound HTTP calls made by those jobs carry a `baggage` header that grows without bound,
composed of entries from many prior, unrelated jobs, until it is large enough to be rejected by downstream services enforcing header size limits.

### Environment
  
 - `Datadog.Trace` v3.x (W3C baggage propagation enabled by default; not present in v2.x)
 - Hangfire background job workers with full APM attached (`CORECLR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1`)
 - Any downstream HTTP service enforcing a maximum combined request header size

### What we believe is happening

#### 1. `Baggage.Current` is a mutable object stored in an `AsyncLocal`

[`Baggage.cs`](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-dotnet/blob/v3.44.0/tracer/src/Datadog.Trace/Baggage.cs)  backs `Baggage.Current` with a single static `AsyncLocal<Baggage>`, where `Baggage` is a mutable  reference type. `AsyncLocal<T>` isolation is copy-on-write on the *reference* — it does not  isolate in-place mutations to the object the reference points to. Calling `MergeInto` on  `Baggage.Current` mutates the shared instance's internal list directly.

#### 2. `OnPerforming` merges extracted baggage into the existing `Baggage.Current`

[`DatadogHangfireServerFilter.OnPerforming`](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-dotnet/blob/v3.44.0/tracer/src/Datadog.Trace/ClrProfiler/AutoInstrumentation/Hangfire/DatadogHangfireServerFilter.cs#L33)  calls [`MergeBaggageInto(Baggage.Current)`](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-dotnet/blob/v3.44.0/tracer/src/Datadog.Trace/Propagators/PropagationContextExtensions.cs),  which adds entries from the extracted job context into `Baggage.Current` without clearing it  first.

#### 3. `OnPerformed` does not reset `Baggage.Current`

[`DatadogHangfireServerFilter.OnPerformed`](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-dotnet/blob/v3.44.0/tracer/src/Datadog.Trace/ClrProfiler/AutoInstrumentation/Hangfire/DatadogHangfireServerFilter.cs#L46)  disposes the span scope only. The  [`AsyncLocalScopeManager`](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-dotnet/blob/v3.44.0/tracer/src/Datadog.Trace/AsyncLocalScopeManager.cs)  uses a completely separate `AsyncLocal<Scope>` with no interaction with `Baggage.AsyncStorage`.  Disposing a scope has no effect on `Baggage.Current`.

#### 4. Hangfire workers reuse the same `ExecutionContext` across sequential jobs

The job dispatch loop in  [`BackgroundProcessDispatcherBuilder.ExecuteProcess`](https://github.com/HangfireIO/Hangfire/blob/main/src/Hangfire.Core/Server/BackgroundProcessDispatcherBuilder.cs)  runs on a dedicated background `Thread` (see  [`BackgroundProcessExtensions.cs`](https://github.com/HangfireIO/Hangfire/blob/main/src/Hangfire.Core/Server/BackgroundProcessExtensions.cs))  in a plain `while` loop calling `Worker.Execute` once per job, with no `ExecutionContext`  operation between iterations. `AsyncLocal` values written during job N are still present when  job N+1 begins.

#### 5. Hangfire's own `AsyncLocal` mitigation does not cover server filters

[`CoreBackgroundJobPerformer.InvokeSynchronously`](https://github.com/HangfireIO/Hangfire/blob/main/src/Hangfire.Core/Server/CoreBackgroundJobPerformer.cs)
shows Hangfire is already aware of this class of problem — it wraps synchronous job method  invocation in `ExecutionContext.Run` specifically to prevent `AsyncLocal` mutations inside the  job body from persisting to future jobs, noting in a comment that without this, such mutations  *"can result in memory leaks and possibly affect future background job method executions in  unexpected ways."*

However, `DatadogHangfireServerFilter.OnPerforming` fires before `InvokeSynchronously`, in  [`BackgroundJobPerformer.InvokeServerFilter`](https://github.com/HangfireIO/Hangfire/blob/main/src/Hangfire.Core/Server/BackgroundJobPerformer.cs), which calls `OnPerforming` before recursing to the inner performer. The `MergeBaggageInto`  mutation therefore occurs on the worker thread's own ambient context, outside any  `ExecutionContext.Run` sandbox.

### Current workarounds

We have applied baggage item and byte caps via `DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_ITEMS` and `DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_BYTES`. These reduce the maximum size of any single extraction but do  not prevent accumulation across jobs — repeated merges can still push the cumulative total past  the cap over time.

We have also tested disabling baggage from the propagation style via `DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE_EXTRACT` and `DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE_INJECT`, which stops the growth but loses baggage-based cross-service correlation.

### Reproduction Code

_No response_

text:
test(release): prove the packaged source candidate and exact published version from clean repositories

Release controller: #2258
Release qualification and platform matrix: #2262
Release-candidate preparation: #2261
Pack substrate/content: #2253/#2254
Walking-skeleton and simplification: #2204/#2208
Native focused proof and receipt: #2207/#2219/#2220/#2221
Release authentication/provenance: #2115/#2047

## Problem

Workspace tests prove source-tree behavior. They do not prove the artifact users install:

- package contents may omit schemas, templates, or selected pack assets;
- manifests may retain workspace-relative assumptions;
- one platform may fail even though Ubuntu CI passes;
- an optional capability may be half-present in help/docs/package data;
- publication may produce a different crate graph than the reviewed candidate;
- process success may hide a missing required proof subject;
- uninstall or rollback may damage unowned files.

The release needs two distinct smoke stages because an exact registry install cannot be verified before publication.

## Outcome

```text
Stage A — SourceCandidateSmoke
  exact reviewed source candidate
  → package/install/run in isolated clean environments
  → protect the irreversible publication boundary

Stage B — RegistryInstallSmoke
  exact published version
  → install from crates.io in fresh environments
  → verify registry artifacts and final release identity
```

Use the same semantic fixture corpus where possible, but never claim Stage B before publication.

## Inputs

Consume the exact #2261 candidate report:

- commit/tree and selected release version;
- ten intended crates and package graph;
- capability matrix;
- claimed platform/MSRV matrix;
- expected package assets;
- selected smoke profiles;
- #2262 qualification digest;
- known exclusions and experimental boundaries.

A changed candidate, capability row, package manifest, required asset, or smoke expectation invalidates the old result.

## Smoke profiles

### Core profile — always required

Exercise the supported exception-ledger product from an isolated temporary Git repository:

```text
--version and help
base doctor / audit
init or use a minimal policy
propose / check --mode no-new / diff
list / explain / worklist
one checked mutation lifecycle fixture
receipt creation and validation
uninstall/cleanup or rollback behavior where applicable
```

The fixture must not rely on the cargo-allow source checkout.

### Spec-led static profile — only when selected

When #2261 marks `SpecLedStaticClaimCompiler` and/or `RIPRStaticTestSeamGrip` as `Experimental`, include only the selected static journey:

```text
one accepted requirement
→ one PR-local implementation claim
→ exact seam and source-declared tests
→ captured/current RIPR static evidence where selected
→ current requirement-purpose posture
```

No external sibling repository is required at install time unless explicitly packaged and selected. The smoke may use a retained native fixture artifact.

### Focused proof profile — only when selected

When `NativeFocusedProofExecution` is selected:

```text
focused proof-plan generation
→ explicit bounded native cargo-allow proof execution
→ discovery/selection/execution/outcome receipt
→ current receipt validation
```

Required negatives:

- zero required subjects selected or executed;
- wrong neighboring test only;
- stale test body/head/plan;
- ignored, skipped, not-found, timed-out, cancelled, and harness-error outcomes;
- process zero with incomplete subject proof.

### Codex pack profile — only when selected

When `CodexPackInstallAndGuidance` is selected:

```text
skills install <built-in pack> --adapter codex --dry-run/apply
skills check and diff
verify lock, ownership, and adapter content
skills remove --dry-run/apply
post-remove doctor/check
```

Assertions:

- issue-first guidance and proportional agent use;
- no fixed persona roster or agent count;
- no repository-global active goal or hidden session pointer;
- one writer per PR/worktree and current-head review guidance;
- no xchecker, Agent Backplane, proofrun, evidencebus, or cockpitctl dependency;
- existing repository-authored instructions/extensions survive install and removal.

The smoke lints and exercises installation; it does not invoke Codex or prove real agent productivity. That evidence belongs to #2257.

## Stage A — source candidate

Run before tag/publication on every platform marked `Supported` or `Experimental` for the corresponding capability.

Required operations:

- `cargo package` all intended crates in dependency order;
- inspect package file lists and normalized manifests;
- reject missing licenses, README, schemas, templates, selected pack assets, or command resources;
- reject path dependencies and source-workspace-only lookups;
- install from the packaged source/candidate artifacts in a fresh `CARGO_HOME` and temporary repository;
- run the selected core and experimental smoke profiles;
- bind results to package checksums, commit/tree, Rust/toolchain, OS, architecture, and capability matrix.

Stage A is the release protection. It must be complete before publication begins.

## Stage B — exact registry version

Run only after all intended crates publish successfully.

For each claimed platform:

- use a new isolated `CARGO_HOME`;
- install exactly the selected release version from crates.io with `--locked` where supported by the release process;
- verify binary version and package graph;
- rerun the selected smoke profiles without source-workspace access;
- verify registry checksums/package identities against #2047;
- classify propagation delay separately from missing/mismatched package;
- emit one exact registry smoke receipt.

A failed Stage B is a release incident. Preserve the failure and resulting correction/yank/follow-up decision; do not rewrite the record as though the first publish succeeded cleanly.

## Platform and MSRV matrix

Run candidate smoke according to #2262/#2261:

```text
Linux
Windows
macOS
Rust 1.85 MSRV lane where claimed
current stable lane
```

A platform/toolchain not executed remains `NotProven` or `NotIncluded` in the release matrix. Do not silently inherit support from another operating system or compiler.

Cross-platform fixtures must compare semantic output for:

- path normalization and separators;
- case-sensitive/case-insensitive edge behavior where relevant;
- CRLF/LF and UTF-8 filenames/content;
- generated artifacts and receipts;
- source-tree inventory ordering;
- package asset discovery;
- install/remove ownership.

Platform-specific metadata may differ only where declared.

## Result contract

Distinguish:

```text
Passed
FindingsAdvisory
FindingsBlocking
NotApplicable
NotProven
PartialData
StaleInput
Unsupported
MalformedInput
InstrumentFailure
Cancelled
TimedOut
Conflict
```

A skipped profile is `NotApplicable` only when its capability is `NotIncluded`. A selected capability whose smoke did not run is `NotProven`, not pass.

## Required negatives

- missing packaged schema/template/pack asset;
- stale or mismatched package version;
- workspace-relative path or symlink dependence;
- package graph with mixed internal versions;
- modified owned pack file or unowned collision;
- uninstall deleting an unrelated file;
- malformed/stale proof receipt;
- zero selected/executed subject;
- hidden network requirement in ordinary offline paths;
- unsupported schema/pack generation;
- platform-specific semantic drift;
- registry package missing or checksum mismatched;
- one stage skipped or cancelled but aggregate reported clean.

## Acceptance

- Stage A passes on every claimed platform/toolchain before publication.
- Every intended package contains the exact required runtime assets.
- The installed candidate runs without the source workspace.
- The core profile passes everywhere claimed.
- Each selected experimental profile passes only where its capability matrix claims support.
- Unselected profiles are absent or clearly not included rather than half-installed.
- Stage B installs and verifies the exact published version on every cl

text:
Database file remains locked after `DocumentDbContext` constructor failure

### Package version

5.0.3

### Affected package

BLite.Core (storage engine)

### .NET version

10.0.201

### Description

## Summary

When `DocumentDbContext` fails during construction (while reading pages and initializing collections), BLite does not release the underlying page file and memory-mapped resources. The database file (and related WAL sidecar files) remain locked by the process even though no usable `DocumentDbContext` instance is returned to the caller.

This report is **not** about the root cause of the exception that triggers the failure. The trigger can be any error during page read or collection bootstrap inside the constructor. In our case, the visible exception is an AES-GCM decryption failure when the configured `ICryptoProvider` password does not match the encrypted store. The bug we are reporting is the **missing cleanup on constructor failure**, which prevents deleting or replacing the database file afterward.

---

## Configuration

```csharp
var config = new PageFileConfig
{
    PageSize = PageFileConfig.Default.PageSize,
    GrowthBlockSize = PageFileConfig.Default.GrowthBlockSize,
    Access = MemoryMappedFileAccess.ReadWrite,
    AllowMultiProcessAccess = true,
    LockTimeout = LockTimeout.From(
        (int)TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15).TotalMilliseconds,
        (int)TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30).TotalMilliseconds
    ),
    CryptoProvider = new AesGcmCryptoProvider(new CryptoOptions(password))
};

// Throws during construction; no instance is returned
var context = new DocumentDbContext(databasePath, config);
```

---

## Impact

| Area | Effect |
|------|--------|
| **Startup recovery** | Host applications that delete and recreate the store after a failed open cannot do so reliably in-process. |
| **Multi-process access** | With `AllowMultiProcessAccess = true`, a failed open in one process can leave files locked and affect sibling processes sharing the same path. |
| **Consumer workarounds** | Callers are forced to use `GC.Collect()`, `GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers()`, rename-to-quarantine fallbacks, or process restart — none of which should be required for correct library behavior. |


### Minimal reproduction

1. Open or create an encrypted database with `AesGcmCryptoProvider` and password **A**.
2. Insert at least one document and call `CheckpointAsync` so collection metadata pages are written.
3. Dispose the context normally (`await DisposeAsync()`).
4. Attempt to open the same database path with password **B** (incorrect password).
5. Observe that `new DocumentDbContext(path, config)` throws before the constructor completes.
6. Without terminating the process, try to delete the database file (and `.wal` / `-shm` sidecars if present).


### Expected behavior

`DocumentDbContext` construction should follow a fail-safe pattern:

1. If any step after `PageFile` / `StorageEngine` initialization throws, all already-acquired native and managed resources (`PageFile`, memory-mapped views, WAL handles, `StorageEngine`, collection managers, etc.) must be disposed **before** the exception propagates to the caller.
2. After the constructor throws, the OS should not retain an exclusive lock on the database file from that failed attempt.
3. Callers should be able to delete or replace the database file in the same process without relying on the finalizer thread or `GC.Collect()`.

This is analogous to the standard IDisposable / IAsyncDisposable contract: a half-initialized object must not leak handles when construction fails.


### Actual behavior

**Actual:** `File.Delete` fails with `IOException` — the file is still in use by the current process. The lock persists until the process exits (or until a non-deterministic GC/finalizer cycle eventually releases handles).

**Expected:** The file can be deleted immediately after the constructor throws, because no open database instance exists.


### Additional context

## Observed exception (trigger only — not the reported bug)

The following stack trace shows where construction fails in our scenario. Any similar failure during `InitializeCollections()` / `ReadPage` would exhibit the same resource leak.

```
System.Security.Cryptography.AuthenticationTagMismatchException:
  The computed authentication tag did not match the input authentication tag.
   at System.Security.Cryptography.AeadCommon.Decrypt(...)
   at System.Security.Cryptography.AesGcm.Decrypt(...)
   at BLite.Core.Encryption.AesGcmCryptoProvider.Decrypt(
        UInt32 pageId, ReadOnlySpan`1 ciphertext, Span`1 plaintext)
   at BLite.Core.Storage.PageFile.ReadPageCore(UInt32 pageId, Span`1 destination)
   at BLite.Core.Storage.PageFile.ReadPage(UInt32 pageId, Span`1 destination)
   at BLite.Core.Storage.StorageEngine.ReadPage(
        UInt32 pageId, Nullable`1 transactionId, Span`1 destination)
   at BLite.Core.Storage.StorageEngine.GetCollectionMetadata(String name)
   at BLite.Core.Indexing.CollectionIndexManager`2..ctor(
        StorageEngine storage, IDocumentMapper`2 mapper, String collectionName)
   at BLite.Core.Collections.DocumentCollection`2..ctor(
        StorageEngine storage, ITransactionHolder transactionHolder,
        IDocumentMapper`2 mapper, String collectionName, FreeSpaceIndex freeSpaceIndex)
   at BLite.Core.DocumentDbContext.CreateCollection[TId,T](IDocumentMapper`2 mapper)
   at BLite.Core.DocumentDbContext.InitializeCollections()
   at BLite.Core.DocumentDbContext..ctor(
        String databasePath, PageFileConfig config, BLiteKvOptions kvOptions)
   at BLite.Core.DocumentDbContext..ctor(String databasePath, PageFileConfig config)
```

---

## Suggested fix direction

- Wrap `DocumentDbContext` constructor body (page file open → storage engine → `InitializeCollections()`) in `try/finally` or use a private initialization helper that disposes partial state on any exception.
- Ensure `PageFile.Dispose()` / `DisposeAsync()` releases the memory-mapped file even when opened but not fully initialized.
- Add a regression test: open encrypted store with wrong password → assert constructor throws → assert database file is not locked (e.g. `File.Delete` succeeds in the same process).

text:
ConnectionPanel: fix auth-flow event-subscription leak (per-Authorize-click handler accumulation)

## Summary
The device-auth flow in `addons/godot_mcp/Editor/UI/ConnectionPanel.cs` (~line 944) subscribes a lambda to `flow.OnStateChanged` but never unsubscribes it when a new device-auth flow replaces the previous `_deviceAuthFlow`. Each "Authorize" click therefore leaks the old flow instance and its closure; subscribed handlers accumulate across repeated clicks.

## Context
Surfaced by the whole-project `/simplify` run on 2026-06-26 (Efficiency agent, finding #1). The codebase already documents the correct leak-fix idiom in `GodotMcpDock.cs` (~line 71) and uses `SerialDisposable` in `GodotMcpConnection.cs`.

## Proposed approach
- Store the `OnStateChanged` handler as a named delegate field and unsubscribe it before replacing `_deviceAuthFlow` (or dispose the prior flow's subscription via a `SerialDisposable`).
- Mirror the existing leak-fix pattern in `GodotMcpDock.cs` / `GodotMcpConnection.cs`.
- Verify the fix does not drop a needed re-subscribe on a legitimate flow restart (bug-adjacent change, not a pure cleanup).
- Single-file fix — keep it tight.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Old auth-flow subscription is released on replacement; no per-click handler accumulation.
- [ ] Build + `Godot-MCP.Tests` (xUnit) + cli suite green in CI.
- [ ] PR opened against `IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP` `main` and merged.

author: JerrettDavis
text:
Generator: Create Observer Pattern

## Summary

Add a **source generator** that produces a complete implementation of the **Observer pattern** for event publication and subscription, with safe-by-default lifetimes and deterministic behavior.

The generator lives in `PatternKit.Generators` and emits code that is:

* reflection-free
* allocation-aware
* explicit about threading policy
* self-contained (no runtime PatternKit dependency)

---

## Motivation / Problem

Observer is easy to misuse:

* leaking subscriptions
* nondeterministic invocation order
* unclear exception behavior (one subscriber breaks others?)
* ad-hoc concurrency policies

We want a generated implementation that makes the “rules of engagement” explicit and testable.

---

## Supported Targets (must-have)

The generator must support:

* `partial class`
* `partial struct`
* `partial record class`
* `partial record struct`

Two consumption modes must be supported:

1. **Event type** (a type represents one observable event stream).
2. **Event hub** (a type groups multiple generated events).

---

## Proposed User Experience

### A) Single event, payload-based

```csharp
[Observer]
public partial class TemperatureChanged { }
```

Generated (representative shape):

```csharp
public partial class TemperatureChanged
{
    public IDisposable Subscribe(Action<Temperature> handler);
    public IDisposable Subscribe(Func<Temperature, ValueTask> handler);

    public void Publish(Temperature value);
    public ValueTask PublishAsync(Temperature value, CancellationToken ct = default);
}
```

### B) Event hub (multi-event grouping)

```csharp
[ObserverHub]
public static partial class SystemEvents
{
    [ObservedEvent]
    public static partial TemperatureChanged TemperatureChanged { get; }

    [ObservedEvent]
    public static partial ShutdownRequested ShutdownRequested { get; }
}
```

Generated semantics:

* Each `[ObservedEvent]` property returns a singleton instance of that event stream.
* Hub generation is optional, but if present must be deterministic and self-contained.

---

## Attributes / Surface Area

Namespace: `PatternKit.Generators.Observer`

### Core

* `[Observer]` on an event stream type
* `[ObserverHub]` on a hub type
* `[ObservedEvent]` on hub properties

### Configuration

`ObserverAttribute` suggested properties:

* `ObserverThreadingPolicy Threading` (default: `Locking`)
* `ObserverExceptionPolicy Exceptions` (default: `Continue`)
* `ObserverOrderPolicy Order` (default: `RegistrationOrder`)
* `bool GenerateAsync` (default: inferred)
* `bool ForceAsync` (default: false)

Enums:

* `ObserverThreadingPolicy`: `SingleThreadedFast`, `Locking`, `Concurrent`
* `ObserverExceptionPolicy`: `Stop`, `Continue`, `Aggregate`
* `ObserverOrderPolicy`: `RegistrationOrder`, `Undefined`

---

## Semantics (must-have)

### Subscriptions

* `Subscribe(Action<T>)` returns an `IDisposable` token.
* `Dispose()` unsubscribes deterministically.
* Duplicate subscriptions are allowed in v1 (invoked multiple times).

### Publishing

* Default order: `RegistrationOrder`.
* Publishing uses **snapshot semantics** (publish iterates a stable snapshot so modifications during publish do not affect the current cycle).

### Exception policies

* `Continue` (default): invoke all handlers; exceptions do not stop others.

  * v1: either swallow exceptions or route them to an optional user hook (see below). Must be explicit.
* `Stop`: first exception aborts.
* `Aggregate`: run all and throw an `AggregateException` (or return a result) at the end.

Recommended v1 behavior:

* For sync `Publish`: `Continue` swallows *by default* but provides an optional hook: `OnSubscriberError(Exception ex)` if present.
* For async `PublishAsync`: same semantics.

### Async

* `Subscribe(Func<T, ValueTask>)` must be supported.
* `PublishAsync` invokes async handlers in deterministic order.
* Cancellation token behavior: best-effort. If canceled before next invocation, stop and return canceled.

### Threading policies

* `SingleThreadedFast`: no locks; documented as not thread-safe.
* `Locking`: lock around subscribe/unsubscribe; publish takes snapshot under lock.
* `Concurrent`: thread-safe with concurrent primitives; ordering may degrade to `Undefined` unless extra work is done. Must be documented.

---

## Optional advanced features (explicitly v2 unless trivial)

* Weak subscriptions
* Backpressure / queueing
* Filters / predicate subscriptions
* “Once” subscriptions

---

## Diagnostics (must-have)

Stable IDs, actionable:

* `PKOBS001` Type marked `[Observer]` must be `partial`.
* `PKOBS002` Hub type marked `[ObserverHub]` must be `partial` and `static`.
* `PKOBS003` Hub property marked `[ObservedEvent]` has invalid shape (must be `static partial` and return the event stream type).
* `PKOBS004` Async publish requested but async handler shape unsupported.
* `PKOBS005` Invalid configuration combination (e.g., `Concurrent` + `RegistrationOrder` requires additional ordering guarantees).

---

## Generated Code Layout

* `TypeName.Observer.g.cs`
* `TypeName.ObserverHub.g.cs` (if hub feature enabled)

Determinism:

* internal storage deterministic where promised (especially for `RegistrationOrder`).

---

## Testing Expectations

* Subscribe/unsubscribe works and is idempotent.
* Publish invokes in registration order.
* Dispose during publish does not break iteration (snapshot semantics).
* Exception policy behavior matches docs:

  * Continue
  * Stop
  * Aggregate
* Threading policy tests:

  * Locking prevents basic races in a concurrent subscribe/publish stress test.
* Async publish respects cancellation (best-effort).

---

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] `[Observer]` works for class/struct/record class/record struct.
* [ ] Supports sync handlers and async handlers (`ValueTask`).
* [ ] Deterministic ordering for `RegistrationOrder` modes.
* [ ] Snapshot publishing semantics.
* [ ] Clear exception policy with tests.
* [ ] Explicit, documented threading policy.
* [ ] Hub mode supported (optional but if implemented, fully tested).
* [ ] Diagnostics cover invalid usage and config.

[Bug]: Memory leak when disposing Krypton.Toolkit.PaletteBase and derived classes.

**Describe the bug**
The class "Krypton.Toolkit.PaletteBase" does not unsubscribe its "OnUserPreferenceChanged" method from the static rooted event "SystemEvents.UserPreferenceChanged", leading to objects persistently maintained in second generation garbage, i.e. memory leaks.

Derived classes also instantiate member controls that do not get disposed and become dangling objects.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start the "TestForm" project.
2. Click on "Buttons" to open the "ButtonsTest" form.
3. Click on the close button.
4. "PaletteBase" objects will not be collected on close.

**Expected behavior**
All "PaletteBase" objects must be garbage collected.

text:
[Problem/Bug]: Memory Leak with some NVIDIA devices causing severe ETW/ETS overrun.

### What happened?

Following a recent WebView2 runtime update, we are observing significant system-wide memory leaks and performance degradation over time during WPF/WebView2 frame rendering.

The issue appears to be an event leak related to NVIDIA filters and ETW/ETS buffers rather than application-level code. Closing the application does not release the leaked memory; however, restarting the application sometimes resets the accumulated event count.

The leaked memory is not bound to a specific process ID because it populates via system events. It likely stems from aggressive tracing being accidentally triggered on the thread. This started occurring globally across installations immediately following a recent WebView2 runtime update.

The memory bias can be forced to clear out by killing the NVIDIA filters via the command line:
```
logman stop "NVIDIA-NVTOPPS-FILTER" -ets
logman stop "NVIDIA-NVTOPPS-NOCAT" -ets
```

We are currently working with our users to collect deeper trace logs (.etl). Because this issue is tied directly to the latest WebView2 runtime behavior and its interaction with NVIDIA's telemetry pipeline, we will likely need upstream input/collaboration from Microsoft and NVIDIA to isolate the exact trace registration registration bug.

You can find our associated tracking issue here: https://github.com/ciderapp/Cider-2/issues/1370

### Importance

Important. My app's user experience is significantly compromised.

### Runtime Channel

Stable release (WebView2 Runtime)

### Runtime Version

145.0.3800.82, and latest as of this issue, 149.0.4022.8

### SDK Version

1.0.3351.48 (This also occurs on the latest SDK version)

### Framework

WPF

### Operating System

Windows 11

### OS Version

26220.8474

### Repro steps

Currently unknown circumstance, although it seems to commonly invoke on the latest NVIDIA driver combined with a subsequent system sleep and wake with the WebView2 application open in the background.

### Repros in Edge Browser

No, issue does not reproduce in the corresponding Edge version

### Regression

Regression in newer Runtime

### Last working version (if regression)

1.0.3351.48, 143.0.3650.139

author: JoonghyunCho
text:
[AI Refactoring] GpsSatellite.SetSatelliteStatusChangeCallback 의 GCHandle.Alloc(this) 미해제 → 구독마다 GCHandle 누수 (userData 미사용) [Scope: src/Tizen.Location] (2026-07-12)

[Type: Refactoring]
[Scope: src/Tizen.Location]
[Priority: 🔴 Critical]
[Lens: Coding Guidelines, Performance]

## Observation
`GpsSatellite.SetSatelliteStatusChangeCallback()` allocates a pinning `GCHandle` for `this` and passes it as the native `userData`, but **never frees it** (`src/Tizen.Location/Tizen.Location/GpsSatellite.cs:278-279`):

```csharp
GCHandle handle = GCHandle.Alloc(this);
int ret = Interop.GpsSatellite.SetSatelliteStatusChangedCallback(
    _handle, _satelliteStatuschangedCallback, _interval, GCHandle.ToIntPtr(handle));
```

The registered callback body **never reads `userData`** — it closes over `_handle` / `_satelliteStatusChanged` directly:

```csharp
_satelliteStatuschangedCallback = (numActive, numInView, timestamp, userData) =>
{
    // ... uses _handle, _satelliteStatusChanged — 'userData' is ignored
    _satelliteStatusChanged?.Invoke(_handle, new SatelliteStatusChangedEventArgs(numActive, numInView, timeStamp));
};
```

`UnSetSatelliteStatusChangeCallback()` frees nothing (rg confirms `GCHandle.Free` appears **nowhere** in the module).

## Problem
- **GCHandle leak (bug risk — missing dispose).** Every time the `SatelliteStatusUpdated` event transitions from 0→1 handlers, a new `GCHandle` is allocated and leaked. Subscribe → unsubscribe → subscribe again leaks one entry from the process-global GCHandle table on each cycle.
- **Object kept alive forever.** `GCHandle.Alloc(this)` is a **strong** handle, so it roots the entire `GpsSatellite` instance for the lifetime of the process — it can never be garbage-collected even after `UnSetSatelliteStatusChangeCallback` and after all app references are dropped.
- **Dead marshalling.** Since the callback never uses `userData`, the handle serves no purpose at all — it is pure leak.

## Proposed Improvement
The `userData` is unused, so drop the `GCHandle` entirely and pass `IntPtr.Zero` (matches every other callback registration in `Locator.cs`, which all pass `IntPtr.Zero`).

### Before
```csharp
GCHandle handle = GCHandle.Alloc(this);
int ret = Interop.GpsSatellite.SetSatelliteStatusChangedCallback(
    _handle, _satelliteStatuschangedCallback, _interval, GCHandle.ToIntPtr(handle));
```

### After
```csharp
int ret = Interop.GpsSatellite.SetSatelliteStatusChangedCallback(
    _handle, _satelliteStatuschangedCallback, _interval, IntPtr.Zero);
```

> (If a future change genuinely needs `userData`, the correct pattern is to store the `GCHandle` in a field and `Free()` it in `UnSetSatelliteStatusChangeCallback()`. But since it is unused today, removing it is the minimal, safe fix.)

### Target Files
- `src/Tizen.Location/Tizen.Location/GpsSatellite.cs`

## Expected Impact (Quantitative Metrics)
- Leaked `GCHandle` entries per subscribe cycle: **1 → 0**.
- Permanently-rooted `GpsSatellite` instances: **1 → 0** (instance becomes collectable again after unsubscribe).

## API Compatibility Check
- Public API signature change: none.
- Behavior change: none observable — `userData` was never read by the callback; the delegate is still kept alive by the `_satelliteStatuschangedCallback` field (unchanged).
- Tizen API Level floor: maintained.

## Impact Scope
- 1 private method, single assembly (`SetSatelliteStatusChangeCallback`, reached only via the internal `SatelliteStatusUpdated` add path).
- No cross-assembly impact.

---

WPF Plot Stops Refreshing Until Mouse Panning Stops

## Bug Report

**Issue:** After a brief time of continuous mouse panning (a second or so) the plot stops refreshing until the mouse stops moving.

**Reproducing:** Click and drag pan constantly (do not let the mouse stop), at first everything refreshes and works but then it stops refreshing and as long as the mouse is kept moving it never redraws, once the mouse stops (even with mouse button not released) it refreshes but has the problem again if panning starts again. The bug is consistently reproducible with a debugger attached to essentially an empty example (see code, axes stop refreshing), or when using the exact same example code in a larger application (without debugger attached). I am not sure why it doesn't happen in all cases. I have investigated and tried toggling/changing all of the configuration quality options (under `WpfPlot.Configuration.Quality` and `WpfPlot.Configuration.QualityConfiguration`) but nothing seems to fix the issue.

This issue is also always reproducible when running the WPF ScottPlot Demo or sandbox/WpfApp in the repository with debugger attached (but does not have the problem when running without debugger). This issue does not seem to be reproducible in WinForms with debugger attached.

I don't mind the problem being present with a debugger attached, but I have the problem without a debugger attached when using ScottPlot.WPF in a larger application.

```cs
public partial class MainWindow : Window
{
    public MainWindow()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        WpfPlot.Plot.Clear();
        WpfPlot.Refresh();
    }
}
```

```xaml
<Window x:Class="GeometryScene.MainWindow"
        xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
        xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
        xmlns:d="http://schemas.microsoft.com/expression/blend/2008"
        xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
        mc:Ignorable="d"
        Title="MainWindow" Height="450" Width="800">
    <Grid x:Name="MainGrid">
        <WpfPlot x:Name="WpfPlot"></WpfPlot>
    </Grid>
</Window>

```

### System Details
* **ScottPlot Version:** 4.1.26
* **Operating System:** Windows 10
* **Application Type:** WPF
* **.NET Version:** NET Framework 4.7.1 or NET Framework 4.8.1

author: doodlemania2
text:
Adopt CommunityToolkit.Mvvm + WPF weak event patterns to fix MVVM and memory-leak antipatterns

## Summary
Adopt the **CommunityToolkit.Mvvm** package and the **WPF weak event pattern** to eliminate two cross-cutting antipatterns: hand-rolled `INotifyPropertyChanged`/`ICommand` boilerplate, and event-handler-induced memory leaks. Companion to the broader refactor in #18.

## 1. Replace hand-rolled MVVM plumbing with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm

### Research
- **Data binding, dependency injection, and unit testing in WinUI — What is the MVVM Toolkit**: ships `ObservableObject`, `RelayCommand`/`AsyncRelayCommand`, `Messenger`, and source-generator attributes that emit boilerplate at compile time, reducing per-property code from ~10 lines to one. Compatible with WPF on .NET Framework. ([learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/tutorials/winui-mvvm-toolkit/intro](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/tutorials/winui-mvvm-toolkit/intro))
- **MVVM Toolkit Features — Source Generators**: `[ObservableProperty]` on a private field generates the public property + change notifications; `[RelayCommand]` on a method generates the `ICommand` wrapper. ([learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/maui/mvvm-community-toolkit-features](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/maui/mvvm-community-toolkit-features#source-generators))
- **MVVMTK0039**: `[RelayCommand]` async methods must return `Task`, not `async void`, so the generator emits an `AsyncRelayCommand` with built-in concurrency control and `IsRunning` tracking. ([learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/communitytoolkit/mvvm/generators/errors/mvvmtk0039](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/communitytoolkit/mvvm/generators/errors/mvvmtk0039))
- **`RelayCommand`/`RelayCommand<T>`**: stable `ICommand` implementation with `CanExecute` change notification — replaces every `Click="..."` handler in `MainWindow.xaml`. ([learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/communitytoolkit/mvvm/relaycommand](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/communitytoolkit/mvvm/relaycommand))

### Antipatterns currently in the repo
- Zero `INotifyPropertyChanged` implementations. State changes are pushed by directly mutating WPF controls from the code-behind (e.g. `StatusText.Text = ...` in `SetStatus`, `Title = ...` in dirty-tracking, `_zoomBox.SelectedItem = ...`). The view and state are coupled and untestable.
- Every button is `Click="..."` in XAML wired to a `private void Foo_Click(object, RoutedEventArgs)` in `MainWindow.xaml.cs` — at least ~30 of them (`ToolSelect_Click`, `ToolText_Click`, `MinimizeBtn_Click`, etc.). No `CanExecute` gating; buttons are enabled/disabled by directly poking `IsEnabled`.

### Implementation
- Add NuGet `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm` (v8.x; `netstandard2.0`, works on `net48`). Cost: a single ~150 KB DLL — Costura will bundle it automatically.
- Introduce VMs (one per dialog + one main):
  ```csharp
  public partial class MainWindowViewModel : ObservableObject
  {
      [ObservableProperty] private string statusText = "";
      [ObservableProperty] private double zoomLevel = 1.0;
      [ObservableProperty] private bool isDirty;
      [ObservableProperty] [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor(nameof(SaveCommand))]
      private bool hasOpenDocument;

      [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(HasOpenDocument))]
      private async Task SaveAsync(CancellationToken ct) { ... }
  }
  ```
- Migrate XAML to `Command="{Binding SaveCommand}"`. The `_xxxBtn = (Button)FindName(...)!` block in the constructor (~L97–110) goes away entirely.
- `[NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor]` replaces every manual `someBtn.IsEnabled = ...` poke (see [MVVMTK0016](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/communitytoolkit/mvvm/generators/errors/mvvmtk0016) for usage).
- Combines with #19 — async commands flow naturally through `[RelayCommand]` on `Task`-returning methods.

## 2. Use weak events for long-lived subscriptions

### Research
- **Weak event patterns**: handlers attached to event sources are not always destroyed in coordination with the listener; the source keeps a strong reference to the listener via the delegate, leaking the listener (and its visual subtree) until the source itself dies. WPF provides `WeakEventManager<TEventSource, TEventArgs>` and the `IWeakEventListener` pattern to break the cycle. ([learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/advanced/weak-event-patterns](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/advanced/weak-event-patterns))

### Where this bites in KillerPDF
- Long-lived sources subscribed to by short-lived UI elements: `_doc` (current document), `_savedSignatures` and the planned `AnnotationStore` (#18) all outlive individual page thumbnails / annotation visuals / dialogs. Once those services start raising `INotifyPropertyChanged` / `INotifyCollectionChanged` after the MVVM refactor, every per-page thumbnail and per-annotation visual will subscribe — and any path that doesn't unsubscribe will pin those visuals in memory for the life of the document.
- Already at risk today: signature popup (`_signaturePopup`), draw-settings bar (`_drawSettingsBar`), and search bar (`_searchBar`) are created/torn down repeatedly and attach handlers to long-lived UI on creation. Verify each has matching `-=` on close.

### Implementation
- For any `INotifyPropertyChanged` / `INotifyCollectionChanged` subscription where the source outlives the listener, subscribe via `WeakEventManager`:
  ```csharp
  PropertyChangedEventManager.AddHandler(annotationStore, OnStoreChanged, nameof(AnnotationStore.IsDirty));
  CollectionChangedEventManager.AddHandler(pages, OnPagesChanged);
  ```
- Audit existing `+=` on long-lived sources from short-lived listeners. Add a one-liner XUnit test (or manual repro) using `WeakReference` to confirm a closed dialog is GC'd.
- The `WM_GETMINMAXINFO` HwndSource hook in `MainWindow_SourceInitialized` is window-scoped and OK as a strong subscription — no change needed there.

## Acceptance
- `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm` referenced; main window plus at least one dialog migrated to VMs in the first PR.
- Zero `Click="..."` handlers remaining in `MainWindow.xaml` after the migration is complete (tracked across multiple PRs).
- Audit script (or one-time manual sweep) confirms no `+=` event subscription from a long-lived service to a short-lived UI element without either `-=` on dispose or a `WeakEventManager` indirection.
- Weak-reference test: open a document, open and close the signature popup 100×, force GC, assert the popup is collected.

## Constraints
- Stay on `net48`. `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm` 8.x targets `netstandard2.0` and works on `net48`. The C# source generators run at compile time and emit code compatible with the target framework — no runtime dependency on Roslyn.
- Keep the single-EXE Costura bundling (`FodyWeavers.xml`) — confirm `CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.dll` ends up embedded.

AIN-9: freeze AI-navigable architecture acceptance

## Parent

[#356 — EPIC: AI Navigability](https://github.com/SuperJMN/RetroSharp/issues/356)

## What to build

Prove the final architecture is easier for fresh agents to navigate and add durable guardrails against the ownership leaks and monolithic test surfaces identified by the epic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent documentation names the deep modules, their interfaces, their seams, and the correct navigation path for common compiler/runtime changes.
- [ ] Architecture tests prevent runtime memory ownership, frontend preparation order, and target SDK emission from leaking back into former modules.
- [ ] The Game Boy and NES monolithic compiler regression files no longer own tests for the extracted modules.
- [ ] CodeGraph can locate each extracted module and its production/test call path without loading a complete target backend.
- [ ] The full solution, repository validation, tracked-ROM dry run, and representative Game Boy/NES builds pass.
- [ ] The parent epic records final measurements and closes only after every child is complete.

## Blocked by

- #359 — AIN-3: Make NES external probes consume the authoritative ABI.
- #360 — AIN-4: Centralize cross-target frontend preparation.
- #362 — AIN-6: Partition Actor Framework generation by domain.
- #363 — AIN-7: Deepen Game Boy SDK lowering.
- #364 — AIN-8: Deepen NES SDK lowering.

## Non-goals

- No arbitrary line-count gate.
- No formatting-only churn.
- No unrelated compiler or runtime feature work.

Ω-OAK-CONVERGENCE-OS V2 — Autonomous Research Factory roadmap

# Ω-OAK-CONVERGENCE-OS V2

## Phrase-mère

Transformer l’écosystème GitHub de Tristan d’un ensemble de PR prudentes mais fragmentées en une usine de convergence qui observe, classe, répare, consolide, vérifie et apprend sans augmenter le bruit ni contourner OAKGate.

## Pourquoi maintenant

PR #351 fournit déjà le noyau dry-run du consolidateur : snapshots typés, graphe de dépendances, chevauchement Jaccard, verdicts OAK⁸, plans de réparation, registre M⁻ et rapports déterministes.

Le prochain incrément ne doit pas créer une autre méta-PR géante. Il doit être livré en micro-PR indépendantes, chacune avec preuve de progrès mesurable.

## Invariants non négociables

- aucun merge, close, rebase, retarget, suppression de branche ou modification de protection automatique;
- aucun affaiblissement d’OAKGate ou conversion d’absence de preuve en PASS;
- aucun nouveau commentaire ou commit pour le même triplet `(PR, head_sha, blocker_signature)`;
- toute mutation doit réduire un bloqueur mesurable ou produire une information réellement nouvelle;
- les PR draft restent draft;
- les chemins sensibles restent sous approbation humaine;
- tout état est lié au head SHA exact, à l’horodatage, au hash du diff et au hash des checks.

## Architecture V2

### 1. Immutable Repository Snapshot

Schéma JSON déterministe :

```json
{
  "repository": "owner/name",
  "observed_at": "RFC3339",
  "base_sha": "sha",
  "pull_requests": [
    {
      "number": 351,
      "head_sha": "sha",
      "diff_hash": "sha256",
      "check_set_hash": "sha256",
      "draft": true,
      "mergeable": true,
      "labels": [],
      "blockers": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Acceptance:
- ordre stable;
- hash reproductible;
- absence de secret ou contenu de diff brut;
- snapshot invalide rejeté fail-closed.

### 2. Blocker Signature + Cooldown Kernel

Identité canonique :

```text
sha256(repo | pr | head_sha | blocker_class | normalized_evidence)
```

Règle :

```text
same head + same blocker signature + no human event = WAIT_COOLDOWN
```

Acceptance:
- zéro commentaire dupliqué sur fixtures répétées;
- changement de SHA ou verdict réactive l’analyse;
- historique M⁻ append-only.

### 3. Exclusive State Machine

Une seule classe primaire par PR :

```text
GREEN_DRAFT
GREEN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED
AUTO_REPAIRABLE
POLICY_BLOCKED
CONFLICTED
MISSING_CHECKS
EXTERNAL_BLOCKED
STALE_OR_SUPERSEDED
WAITING_ON_PARENT
UNKNOWN
```

Axes secondaires séparés :

```text
state/*
gate/*
risk/*
action/*
```

Acceptance:
- jamais deux `state/*` simultanés;
- labels historiques séparés du statut courant;
- transitions illégales rejetées.

### 4. Dependency-Centrality Scheduler

Priorité proposée :

```text
priority = 4*descendants_blocked
         + 3*reusable_utility
         + 2*expected_backlog_reduction
         - repair_complexity
         - sensitivity_cost
```

Acceptance:
- les racines de stacks passent avant leurs descendants;
- cycles rejetés;
- ties résolus de façon déterministe;
- aucune priorité présentée comme preuve de qualité scientifique.

### 5. Progress-Gated Action Planner

Classes d’issue d’exécution :

```text
CONVERGED
BLOCKER_REDUCED
INFORMATION_GAINED
STATE_ONLY_UPDATED
NO_PROGRESS
REGRESSION
```

Une mutation n’est autorisée que si :

```text
expected_blocker_reduction > 0
OR new_information_score >= threshold
```

Acceptance:
- un rapport répétitif devient `NO_PROGRESS`;
- un test qui élimine un défaut devient `BLOCKER_REDUCED`;
- un simple label devient `STATE_ONLY_UPDATED`;
- aucune action n’est présentée comme réparation sans delta mesuré.

### 6. WIP and Stack Budget

Mode convergence lorsque :

```text
open_pr_count > open_pr_target
```

Politique initiale :

```text
open_pr_target: 8
deep_work_in_progress_limit: 3
max_scientific_stacks: 2
max_governance_meta_prs: 1
```

Le système ne ferme rien automatiquement. Il produit uniquement :

```text
KEEP_ACTIVE
WAITING_ON_PARENT
CONSOLIDATE_CANDIDATE
SUPERSEDED_CANDIDATE
ARCHIVE_CANDIDATE
```

### 7. Merge-Approval Queues

Trois sorties humaines seulement :

```text
A_READY_FOR_READINESS_APPROVAL
B_READY_FOR_MERGE_APPROVAL
C_HUMAN_REPAIR_REQUIRED
```

Aucune promotion automatique de draft et aucun auto-merge dans V2.

### 8. Convergence Dashboard

Métriques obligatoires :

```text
open_pr_count
merged_7d
unblocked_7d
median_pr_age
median_red_to_green_time
repeated_blocker_count
diagnostic_commits_without_reduction
blocked_stack_count
merged_to_generated_ratio
convergence_ratio
```

Formule principale :

```text
convergence_ratio =
  (merged_prs + materially_unblocked_prs)
  / max(1, created_prs + mutated_prs)
```

## Plan de livraison en micro-PR

### V2.1 — Snapshot + schemas
- snapshot schema;
- blocker-signature schema;
- deterministic fixtures;
- hash and validation tests.

### V2.2 — State machine + cooldown
- exclusive primary state;
- transition table;
- duplicate-action suppression;
- M⁻ append-only tests.

### V2.3 — Dependency scheduler
- descendant centrality;
- stack root ranking;
- cycle and tie tests;
- no scientific-superiority claims.

### V2.4 — Progress gate + dashboard
- action outcome classifier;
- convergence metrics;
- JSON and Markdown summaries;
- regression fixtures.

### V2.5 — Read-only GitHub adapter
- separate sensitive PR;
- read-only permissions;
- no label/comment mutation;
- provenance manifest;
- explicit OAKGate review.

## Benchmark minimal

Fixture repository containing :

- une PR draft verte;
- une PR non-draft verte nécessitant approbation;
- une PR bloquée par `GITHUB-001`;
- une PR conflictuelle;
- une PR sans checks;
- une stack parent → enfant → petit-enfant;
- deux PR fortement chevauchantes;
- une PR supersédée avec delta unique non nul;
- une répétition exacte du même snapshot.

Succès V2 :

- classification exacte et déterministe;
- aucune mutation externe;
- aucun diagnostic dupliqué;
- racine de stack priorisée;
- métriques de convergence reproductibles;
- rapport identique à entrée identique, hors champ temporel explicitement isolé.

## M⁻ anti-répétition

1. `diagnostic_artifact != blocker_reduction`.
2. `generic_ci_green != policy_gate_green`.
3. `mergeable != safe_to_merge`.
4. `same_sha + same_blocker = cooldown`.
5. `new_feature_pr > root_stack_repair` est interdit en mode convergence.
6. `priority_score != scientific_truth`.
7. `automation_green != human_impact_safe`.

## Définition de fini

Cette issue est complétée seulement lorsque les quatre couches non sensibles V2.1–V2.4 sont intégrées avec tests, puis que V2.5 possède une revue OAK explicite séparée. Aucun succès n’est revendiqué sur la seule base de documentation ou de CI générique verte.

## Liens

- Parent conceptuel : PR #351
- Séparation workflow sensible : issue #350

Investigate guarded Timberborn startup exit after Steam-frontmost recovery

# Investigate guarded Timberborn startup exit after Steam-frontmost recovery

## Context

#76 successfully added and live-accepted the guarded startup retry cadence: one helper-owned `open_bundle`, no duplicate rapid relaunch, and successful `latest_save_startup_complete` in the acceptance run.

After #76 merged into `main`, #64 still hit a fair-run blocker during the single Live QA Controller path. This was not a duplicate-launch failure: the helper recorded one guarded launch/open-bundle intent, then stayed Steam-frontmost and ended with Timberborn exited before `latest_save_startup_complete` or command bridge status.

## Latest Evidence

#64 post-#76 rerun artifact root:

- `/tmp/wildfire-qa/live-controller-20260531/twf-64-94d33468-post76-rerun`

Important transcripts:

- Deploy passed: `/tmp/wildfire-qa/live-controller-20260531/twf-64-94d33468-post76-rerun/commands/01-deploy-64.txt`
- Startup failed: `/tmp/wildfire-qa/live-controller-20260531/twf-64-94d33468-post76-rerun/commands/02-guarded-launch-from-main.txt`

Key failure tokens:

```text
startup_intent mode=launch timberborn_running=false action=open_bundle
startup_success process_running=true launched=true was_running_before_launch=false activation_status=activated
Expected Timberborn foreground ... got frontmost_bundle_id=com.valvesoftware.steam
startup_failure failure_kind=timberborn_process_exit process_running=false frontmost_bundle_id=com.valvesoftware.steam
launch_intent_failure_recorded failure_kind=timberborn_process_exit ... cooldown_ms=240000
```

`pgrep -xfl Timberborn` was empty after the failure. The `qa-fixture-readiness stored-goods` command never ran, so this is an environment/startup blocker rather than product evidence for #64.

## Goals

- Determine why Timberborn sometimes exits after the guarded helper records a successful launch but before known-screen detection or command bridge readiness.
- Distinguish Steam/frontmost/focus churn from actual Timberborn process exit/crash.
- Add diagnostics or guardrails that make the next failure actionable without issuing repeated helper launches.
- Preserve the single Live QA Controller rule: avoid parallel launch threads and duplicate rapid `open_bundle` attempts.

## Suggested Investigation

- Compare the successful #76 acceptance transcript with the failing #64 post-#76 transcript.
- Inspect newest `Player.log` and any Timberborn error-report zip after the failed #64 run.
- Check whether the helper should capture process exit code, Steam app state, launch marker PID liveness, or a focused error-report snapshot when `failure_kind=timberborn_process_exit`.
- Audit any QA controller safe-close/process checks that could self-match shell command text; use `pgrep -xfl Timberborn` or equivalent exact-process checks.

## Verification

- Deterministic tests for any startup-helper diagnostic changes.
- A single guarded live run is sufficient for acceptance: either reaches `latest_save_startup_complete`, or fails with clearer process-exit evidence and no second `startup_intent ... action=open_bundle`.

## Role

Researcher or Worker, depending on whether the first pass finds a clear helper/tooling change.
